# Exact cap for the fixed-half-mass triangle selector test

This note proves the geometric and cap part of a candidate obstruction
to the fixed-mass moment-body centroid rule. The statement about the
moment body's centroid is a SEPARATE certification obligation until its
rational enclosure proof has been audited. Nothing here refutes OC.

Let K be the triangle in R^2 with vertices

    v0=(-1/3,-1/3), v1=(2/3,-1/3), v2=(-1/3,2/3).

Write

    a=1/8, c=257/256, delta=1-(a+c)/2=223/512,
    s=delta v0=(-223/1536,-223/1536).

At integer bases -1,0,1 prescribe the fibers

    K_- = s+aK, K_0=K, K_+ = s+cK.

Their convex hull C in R x R^2 has exactly these integer fibers.
Indeed the extreme-base sections are fixed by convexity, and

    (K_-+K_+)/2 = delta v0 +(1-delta)K subset K.

Every point of the middle section of the hull can be grouped into a
convex combination of K and the displayed midpoint set. Thus the
middle section is exactly K. The base projection is [-1,1], with no
other sampled integers. A full triangle in one base and any point in
another base span R^3, so C is a convex body. All three sampled fibers
have positive area; q=d=2 and the intrinsic measure is their area sum.

The masses and prescribed fixed half-mass are

    |K_-|=1/128, |K_0|=1/2, |K_+|=66049/131072,
    M=132609/131072, t=M/2=132609/262144.

Both endpoint masses are less than t. Hence the only weighted median
base is zero. More strongly, the moment body B_t(j) is EMPTY at either
endpoint j: a dominated submeasure whose base mean is an extreme base
must lie in that fiber, whose total area is less than t. There are no
other possible sampled bases. The middle moment body is feasible,
because its maximum balanced mass is

    1/2+2(1/128)=33/64 > t.

The configuration is invariant under swapping x1 and x2. Its middle
moment body and, if positive-dimensional, its area centroid inherit
that symmetry. Write this centroid as (h,h).

Consider the SINGLE FIXED CLOSED ambient halfspace

    H={ (z,x): -x1-x2 >= 1/125 +(91357/96000) z }.

If h<=-1/250, then (0,h,h) belongs to H. The cap calculation below is
exact and does not require equality with the cap boundary.

Put u=(-1,-1). On K the range of u.x is [-1/3,2/3]. On K_+ its maximum
is

    u.s+2c/3 = 223/768+514/768 = 737/768.

The threshold of H at z=1 is exactly 737/768. The intersection is the
one extremal vertex and has zero area. On K_- the minimum is

    u.s-a/3=191/768.

The threshold at z=-1 is -90589/96000<191/768. Thus H contains the
whole small endpoint triangle and receives mass 1/128 there.

On the middle triangle H is a vertex cap homothetic to K with linear
ratio (2/3-1/125)/(2/3+1/3)=247/375. Its area is therefore

    (1/2)(247/375)^2.

Consequently

    mu(H)=1/128 +(1/2)(247/375)^2=4045201/18000000,
    (gamma_2/2) M=(2/9)M=44203/196608,
    (gamma_2/2) M-mu(H)=872713/9216000000>0.

Thus a rigorous certificate h<=-1/250 would refute the fixed
t=M/2^n moment-body centroid selector, even with an existential choice
of feasible integer base: only the middle base is feasible. It would
also refute choosing among these bodies by maximum marginal depth or
maximum volume. The original OC conclusion could still hold at another
point of the middle fiber, and is not challenged by this selector test.
